search_strategy: Methodical and source-ordered but with real gaps. The agent cloned the repo, read the four ticket files, then worked wiki -> mail -> chat in that order. Wiki: it found the three directly relevant pages (132/134/133) via /api/search and — critically — fetched each one's full JSON including comments (not just /api/search snippets), so it correctly picked up the 3 wiki-comment clues despite the task's warning that search does not index comments. Mail: it dumped ALL 142 messages to a local file up front and grepped/read offline, which is why every one of the 5 mail-carried clues was found (100% mail recall). Chat: this is where the run leaked. It started by hitting the 4 channels that Mattermost's own text search surfaced early (pipeline, releases, code-review, viewer) and dumped and grepped those thoroughly — these account for the large majority of found clues. It never enumerated the channel list itself until step ~93 (very late, after the code was already committed, pushed, and deployed), at which point it discovered #cookbooks, #general, #incidents, #help, #engineering, #off-topic, #random and #town-square existed. Of these it dumped only engineering, incidents and help — #cookbooks and #general were never dumped at all — and grepped that batch with a narrow, already-known term list ('max_output_bytes|output_cap|truncated_streams|elided|capped') that misses plain-English phrasing like 'output cap' (no underscore) and topically-disguised remarks like say26 ('field_validator'/'ValidationError' with no cap-related token at all). #cookbooks alone held 6 of the 46 remarks, including the three that would have fixed both lost facts (OutputCapError's name, its .max_bytes attribute, and 'the except handler logs nothing'). No Gitea issues or PRs were found relevant (correctly — none exist for this ticket) and the WS-033 design page was checked and correctly judged irrelevant to the byte-level details.
end_reason: n/a — the run completed normally: code committed (b43e8c7), CI green, service deployed and health-checked, task marked complete. Both lost facts were pure retrieval gaps, not a broken run.
notable: The single biggest structural finding: #cookbooks (6 remarks: l-floor-nikolai, l-floor-konrad, l-log-konrad, l-scope-1, l-rule-3, g2.r2.rev1) was never dumped in 98 steps, and both facts this run lost trace directly to remarks that lived only there (line 5234 shows the channel existed and was known to the agent by name at the very end, but it was excluded from even the final catch-up dump).

The final 'let me make sure I haven't missed anything' sweep (transcript line 5227-5279) happened AFTER git push (line 4983) and AFTER CI went green (line 5032) — so even a lucky late find could not have changed the shipped commit without another push, which never happened.

The agent caught and self-corrected one of its own premature readings: at line 1216 it initially concluded the OLD (herring) marker-inside-budget rule was still live from a single mail sentence, then read the rest of the same thread and corrected itself by line 1719 — a good example of not stopping at the first plausible reading.

All 4 herrings were seen and correctly resisted; for g2.r2.h1 the agent never even saw its explicit reversal (also stuck in #cookbooks) but avoided it anyway because two independent, earlier sources (wiki pages 132/133, read in the first 10 steps) had already settled the same correct answer — a case where redundant planting saved the fact despite one path failing.

The observability bug is a genuine, demonstrable double-log: the shipped code caps and logs once inside the try block's normal exit path, and again inside the except handler, so a run whose stdout was already capped before __exit__ raises reports the warning twice instead of once.
